goal: The runner asks GitHub what is open before it acts, and lands through one door. Two sentences, three steps.

Measured on 2026-09-02: seven step runs, five ending `plan-trespass`, six pull requests left open, one step squash-merged into a branch that was not `main` and logged `success,merged`, and a 120-minute session started at 04:33 to rebuild a step whose work was already open as #11241.
contract: The runner starts no step for a project that has an open pull request.
Every merge the runner makes goes through `mc merge`. No `gh pr merge` anywhere in `run.js` (Martin, 2026-09-02).
Nothing here spends a session or a model on an unlanded pull request; every repair is deterministic code. `reconcile` is the exception that already exists and is not touched.
A session that changed a field it may not touch keeps its pull request open and its project stopped until Martin has seen it. The runner never rewrites such a plan file on the session's behalf.
out_of_scope: How `reconcile` resolves conflicts, and when it runs.
Closing or landing by hand the pull requests that are open today. Step 3 measures what the finished runner does with whatever is still open then; it does not tidy them.
memoro, except the mechanical plan migration in step 3.

success_criteria.criterion: The runner starts no step for a project that has an open pull request.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run.test.js`: plan `ready` on main, one open pull request on a `<name>-…` branch, `deps.session` never called, the log line names the pull request. Then live — with #11246 open, `mc run --once` starts no `action-window` step; read the line in `~/mc/runner/log/runner.log`.

success_criteria.check: `mc --fresh` prints #11246 on the `action-window` row and `mc status action-window` names it. Read in the terminal — today the collector matches `headRefName === name` and prints nothing for a project whose three branches all have one open.

success_criteria.criterion: A session is never started on a branch it cannot push to.
success_criteria.check: A test: a worktree whose branch is contained in `origin/main` is moved to `<name>-<n>` from `origin/main` before the session starts. Then live, on a workarea standing on a landed branch — its runs.tsv row carries a pull request number rather than `-`.

success_criteria.check: `grep -n 'pr., .merge' src/mc/run.js` returns nothing, and a test shows the gated round is what a finished step calls. A red gate leaves the pull request open and the project stopped.

success_criteria.criterion: A plan that cannot be read on `origin/main` is raised where somebody looks.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: A landed branch is the normal state of a workarea, not an accident
body: The step was written from one workarea — `action-window`, standing on a branch `origin/main` had already swallowed. Asked of every workarea under `~/mc` on 2026-09-02 with `branchLanded`, 44 of them stand on a branch whose content is already in `origin/main`, in both repositories — and this project's own workarea was one of them: `runner-open-prs` carries merged #516, so the push-guard would have refused this step's own push the moment it tried to open a pull request. The move to `<name>-<n>` is therefore not a repair for one bad night; it is what almost every workarea's next round will do on its first pass, and the `<name>-<suffix>` convention the matcher rests on is about to become true forty-four times over.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: The three places the runner reads were never in disagreement — nobody had asked the third
body: Live on 2026-09-02: 39 plans across the two origin/mains, 16 open pull requests, and four of the six `ready` projects each waiting on one of them (`action-window` #11246, `email-window-layout` #11247, `inbox-finish` #11248, `msr-track-3` #11249). Every one of those pull requests sits on a branch named `<name>` or `<name>-<suffix>`; the old matcher, `headRefName === name`, found nothing at all for `action-window`, whose branch is `action-window-step5`. The convention held everywhere before anything enforced it, which is why the longest-name rule needs no second rule for a case nobody has seen.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: A `gh` that cannot answer is a third state, and this step chose to stop on it
body: The contract says the runner starts no step for a project that has an open pull request. When `gh pr list` fails — no auth, no network — the runner does not know, and the plan does not say what to do with not knowing. Decided in the code: the repository whose answer failed starts nothing that round, with one line saying so, and the other repository's lane is untouched. An idle round costs ten minutes of sleep; a blind one bought a 120-minute Opus session on 2026-09-02. `queue()` returns `prsFailed` for this, and step 2 meets the same question when the gated round cannot reach GitHub.

documents.label: The merge door and its gate

steps.title: A round asks GitHub before it acts
steps.done_when: An open pull request on a project ends that project's round with a line naming it, and a workarea whose branch has already landed is moved to a fresh branch before any session is started.
instruction: The runner looks in two places — `origin/main` for the queue (`run.js:807`) and the worktree for the plan it acts on (`run.js:237`) — and asks GitHub about pull requests exactly once, *after* the session (`run.js:761`). So a step whose work is sitting in an open pull request is still `ready` everywhere the runner reads. On 2026-09-02T04:33 that started a 120-minute Opus session to rebuild `action-window` step 4 while step 4's work was open as #11241: the workarea's worktree stood on a branch `origin/main` had already swallowed, so the plan it read said `ready`. A third place to look is the whole fix.

Write `src/mc/project-prs.js`. `projectForBranch(branch, names)` returns the longest name in `names` that equals `branch` or that `branch` begins with followed by a hyphen, null otherwise. Longest wins because `mc`, `mc-cut`, `mc-log` and `mc-test` are all project names, and `mc-cut-2` resolving to `mc` would attach a pull request to the wrong project. This rests on a convention — a project's branches are `<name>` or `<name>-<suffix>` — which holds for every open pull request on 2026-09-02 and which the second half of this step makes true by construction. Say in the module header that a pull request on a differently named branch is invisible to this; do not add a second rule to cover a case nobody has seen.

The open pull requests are already asked for once per repository, but only by the page: `page-collect.js:464`, `gh pr list --state open --limit 100 --json number,headRefName`. Add `baseRefName,isDraft,title`, and make `run.js`'s `queue()` ask the same question once per repository per round, returning it beside `plans`. `queue()` is re-read per lane and already runs a `git fetch` there, so this is one `gh` call where the network is already being paid for. Then use the matcher at `page-collect.js:233`, which matches `headRefName === name` today and therefore shows no pull request at all for `action-window` while three of its branches have one open.

The rule itself: in `runStep`, after the tmux and dirty-worktree checks and before the kind is chosen, a non-empty answer from `openPrsFor` means this round is over for that project. Say `<name>: #<n> is open (<title>) — not starting a step` and return `'skipped'`. Put the decision in `run-plan.js` beside `chooseKind` — `chooseKind({ plan, conflicts, openPrs })` returning `{ kind: null, reason: 'in-flight', skip: … }` — so it is proved without spending a session. A draft counts as open.

This one rule also covers the two cases nothing else does: a session that timed out with commits pushed and no pull request (`no-json`, rc 143, 04:34 that morning), and a step that ended `plan-trespass`. Both leave a branch carrying unlanded work, and today's runner comes back the next round, reads the worktree's plan, finds the next step ready and builds on top of it — which is how #11250 came to exist.

The second half of the step, in the same place in `runStep` and for the same reason: before a session is started, the worktree must be somewhere it can push from. `branch-landed.js` answers whether a branch's content is already in `origin/main` — by content, because the runner squash-merges and "ahead by N commits" says nothing. If it has landed, check out a new branch from `origin/main` named `<name>-<n>`, the smallest `<n>` for which no branch of that name exists locally or on the remote. The `action-window` workarea stood on `action-window`, merged as #11177 and deleted on the remote; had that 04:33 session finished, the push-guard (`src/mc/push-guard.js`, D-0164) would have refused its push and the whole session would have bought nothing. The guard asks the right question at the wrong end. Leave a workarea whose branch has *not* landed exactly where it is — that branch carries work, and the rule above has already decided what happens to it.

Do not read the plan out of the open pull request. The queue stays built from `origin/main`; `mc status` saying `ready` while the truth is `waiting on #<n>` is closed by the line the page prints, not by giving the runner a fourth source of truth to disagree with itself about.

steps.title: The runner lands only through `mc merge`
steps.done_when: `run.js` calls no `gh pr merge`; a finished step's pull request is landed by the gated round, and a merge that did not land on `main` is not recorded as merged.
instruction: `mergePr` (`run.js:290`) squash-merges with `gh pr merge --squash` and waits only for `mergeable`. Two things follow. A step lands without the gate — while `repo-merge.js`'s own header says there is no way to merge a red gate, "not a flag, not an option, not an environment variable". And the base is never read: on 2026-09-02 at 13:00 that merged #11250 into `msr-track-3-capture-command`, the branch of #11249 which the runner itself had left open eighty minutes earlier, logged `success,merged`, and `main` received nothing. Martin, 2026-09-02: only `mc merge` may be used.

So delete `mergePr`'s merge and call the gated round instead — `repo-merge.js` in process, not by shelling out to `mc`, since the runner is mc. Read what that round already gives you before writing anything: it takes a lease and holds it across the whole round, freshens the branch against its base, re-checks that the ground has not moved between the measurement and the merge, and reports `merged_into` and `off_default` — fields that exist *because* a round on #363 said "merged as 7dcbf96" and was right, into `pm-heartbeat`, its stacked base, and everyone read "on main". The runner's job is to read those two fields rather than to believe its own `success,merged`.

A red gate is not a failure to work around. The pull request stays open, the runs.tsv note says the gate was red, and step 1's rule then keeps that project from starting anything else until it is dealt with.

The gate costs a round — 20–35 minutes on memoro — where the old merge cost seconds. That is the price of the contract and it is not to be optimised away here. Log the landing's own time separately from the session's `seconds` so a reader of runs.tsv can see where a night went.

A stack is the one case that needs an order rather than a call. `mc merge` refuses a batch aimed at several bases, and memoro's `AGENTS.md` § *Landing a stack* is the recipe, measured on a three-step memoro-cli stack on 2026-09-01: land the bottom, `gh pr edit <n> --base main` on the one above it, then `git rebase --onto origin/main <the old base's head>` on its branch — because a squashed base leaves every branch above it conflicting even when its author did nothing wrong; both remaining branches went from `MERGEABLE` to `CONFLICT (content)` the moment the first landed. Then land it. Order the project's open pull requests by base first: the one aimed at `main` is the bottom, each other one's base names the branch below it. Two aimed at `main`, a cycle, or a base that is nobody's head is not a stack the runner understands — say so and land none. Put the ordering in `run-plan.js` as a pure function over the list step 1 already fetches, so the whole decision is tested with no network.
A rebase that conflicts is not resolved here and is not what `reconcile` is for. `git rebase --abort`, say which files conflicted, leave the branch as it was, and stop on that project for the round.

steps.title: What a session leaves in the plan file
steps.done_when: `steps[i].learned` has replaced the top-level `what_the_code_taught_us` everywhere, a plan that does not parse on `origin/main` has a row in `~/mc/intake/`, and the close-out is written.
instruction: Five of the seven step runs on 2026-09-02 ended `plan-trespass` and three of them were not trespasses: `what_the_code_taught_us[0].body: at least one paragraph` (`email-window-layout`), `what_the_code_taught_us[0]: must be an object` (`inbox-finish`), and the same fault on `new-user`, whose plan has sat unreadable on `origin/main` since. Prose in a schema-validated file, where the wrong shape invalidates the whole plan, is prose in the wrong place. Martin's ruling, 2026-09-02: move it into the step.

In `plan-schema.js`: remove `what_the_code_taught_us` and `validateLessons`; add `learned` to `STEP_KEYS` as prose — an array of paragraph strings, possibly empty, the shape `goal`, `contract` and `instruction` already use. `unauthorisedChanges` then gets simpler rather than more complicated: everything a step session may write is inside `steps[index]` — `status`, `pr`, `learned` — plus `met` on the criteria it met. A comparison of one index replaces a comparison of a shared field.

Then migrate: 37 plans on memoro's `origin/main` and one here (`docs/project/mc/mc-cut/PLAN.json`) carry the key, most with it empty. Write it as a one-off script under `scripts/`, run it, commit the result — do not hand-edit 38 files. An entry `{ title, body }` becomes paragraphs on the step it belongs to; where it does not say which, put it on the last `done` step, and where none is done, on the first. Say in the pull request how many entries moved and where the ambiguous ones went. The migration conflicts with every step pull request open at that moment, so check `mc` first and land it when the board is quiet.

The places that describe the field must move together or the next session reads the old shape: `run-plan.js`'s `stepPrompt`, `canon/roles/step.md`, `docs/project/README.md` in *both* repositories, `docs/technical/mc-plan.md`, and `canon/coding-agent-protocol.md` with its copy at `docs/coding-agent-protocol.md`.

While the prompt is open, state the two shapes it has never stated. `stepPrompt` names the fields a session may write and never says what they look like — the schema is only in `docs/project/README.md`, which a headless session has not read. Say inline that `blocked` requires `blocked_by: { kind: "decision" | "project", name }`, which `action-window` got wrong at 10:18, and that a criterion's own text is Martin's while only `met` is the session's, which `msr-track-3` got wrong at 12:27. Do not make `blocked_by` optional: a blocked step that does not say what it waits for is a step nobody can unblock. The boundary itself does not move — `unauthorisedChanges` still refuses a session that touched `goal`, `contract`, `out_of_scope`, another step, or a criterion's text, and by step 1 that project then starts nothing more.

The third case in the same family is a plan that cannot be read at all. `chooseKind` already returns `{ reason: 'unparseable', … }` and `runStep` prints it to `runner.log`, which nobody reads: `new-user` has had that line every round for a day and has, as far as the board shows, stopped being a project. Write it where the unplanned workareas go — `close-workarea.js` has the pattern in `unplannedRow`/`unplannedFile`, a table rewritten whole each round so a fixed project leaves the list by itself. One row per project: name, repository, first problem, plan path. Raise it in `mc brief --collect` beside the other things a machine must not decide.

Close-out. `docs/technical/mc-run.md` gains the round's decision order (an open pull request ends the round; a landed branch is replaced; otherwise the step), the `<name>-<n>` convention the matcher depends on, and that landing is `mc merge` and nothing else. Add the row to `docs/project/project_log.md`. Delete rulings 5 and 6 from `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` — a ruling lives only until the code carries it. Then measure the thing this project was for against the real board: read `~/mc/runner/log/runs.tsv` from the day step 1 landed and count the rows ending `success,open` or `plan-trespass` and the open pull requests they left; on 2026-09-02 it was five trespasses and six pull requests in one day. Put the number in this step's `learned` and set the plan `done`.
